open_points.subject: 30_modules.md:`bindings`
open_points.text: These are the modules `bindings` depends on, not the symbols it imports
open_points.question: Does every module named under `bindings` → Knows require a `module_internal` dependency edge, or is this only an allow-list from which `module_internal` may omit providers whose symbols the implementation does not directly name?
options: Every listed module must have a `module_internal` edge with at least one symbol
The list is only an architectural allow-list; actual dependency edges are exactly those in `module_internal`
The list records a second kind of dependency independent of the import graph
open_points.default_guess: Treat the list as an architectural allow-list and make `module_internal` the sole actual dependency graph.

witness.initial: `bindings` lists `clock` as a module it depends on, but no `imports.module_internal.bindings.clock` entry or directly named clock symbol is supplied.
events: One implementer treats every listed module as a mandatory dependency and adds a clock edge.
Another implementer treats the list as permitted knowledge and omits the clock edge unless the eventual code directly names a clock export.
outcomes: The slicer and affected-set include `clock` as a dependency of `bindings`.
The slicer and affected-set do not include `clock` as a dependency of `bindings`.
witness.observer: A maintainer changing `clock`, and the projector constructing the local spec

open_points.subject: 30_modules.md:`bindings`
open_points.text: which models, enums and interfaces of `models` its code names is fixed by its `imports.module_internal` (SPEC_STANDARD §7), not by this list.
open_points.question: Who owns `imports.module_internal.bindings.models`, and what exact minimal set of model, enum and interface symbols must it contain before the `bindings` code and contracts are written?
options: State 3 fixes the exact symbol set now
A later contract state fixes signature types and State 3 separately fixes additional runtime-named model symbols
The code author chooses the symbols while implementing `bindings`
open_points.default_guess: Derive a minimal set from the eventual contracts and direct runtime references, even though that silently lets the later contract and code authors decide the boundary.

witness.initial: The owned binding behavior requires reading manifest operations, creating and accepting bindings, and checking status, but no `module_internal` entry names the model symbols available to the module.
events: One implementer designs `bindings` to directly construct and test the relevant models and enums and declares them in `module_internal`.
Another implementer moves those constructions or comparisons behind provider functions and declares fewer model symbols.
outcomes: `bindings` has direct runtime imports and knowledge of the selected model and enum types.
`bindings` has a narrower model dependency and delegates the same behavior through other module APIs.
witness.observer: The generated `bindings` module, dependency graph, and later agents extending or testing its boundary

open_points.subject: 30_modules.md:`flows`
open_points.text: These are the modules `flows` depends on, not the symbols it imports
open_points.question: Does every module named under `flows` → Knows require a `module_internal` dependency edge, or is this only an allow-list from which `module_internal` may omit providers whose symbols the implementation does not directly name?
options: Every listed module must have a `module_internal` edge with at least one symbol
The list is only an architectural allow-list; actual dependency edges are exactly those in `module_internal`
The list records a second kind of dependency independent of the import graph
open_points.default_guess: Treat the list as an architectural allow-list and make `module_internal` the sole actual dependency graph.

witness.initial: `flows` lists `clock` and `canonical_values` as dependencies, but no corresponding `module_internal` entries or directly named symbols are supplied.
events: One implementer creates edges for every module in the Knows list.
Another implementer creates only the edges required by the particular proof and activation implementation.
outcomes: Changes to every listed provider place `flows` in the affected-set.
Only providers whose exports are directly used place `flows` in the affected-set.
witness.observer: A maintainer changing a listed provider, and the projector constructing the local spec

open_points.subject: 30_modules.md:`flows`
open_points.text: which models, enums and interfaces of `models` its code names is fixed by its `imports.module_internal` (SPEC_STANDARD §7), not by this list.
open_points.question: Who owns `imports.module_internal.flows.models`, and what exact minimal set of model, enum and interface symbols must it contain before the `flows` code and contracts are written?
options: State 3 fixes the exact symbol set now
A later contract state fixes signature types and State 3 separately fixes additional runtime-named model symbols
The code author chooses the symbols while implementing `flows`
open_points.default_guess: Derive a minimal set from the eventual contracts and direct runtime references, even though that silently lets later agents decide whether proof and activation logic directly names particular models and enums.

witness.initial: `flows` must compose, prove and activate versions and compare effect and disclosure classes, but no `module_internal` entry identifies the model and enum symbols its runtime code may name.
events: One implementer imports and directly operates on flow, proof, activation, effect-class and disclosure-class models.
Another implementer receives primitive or provider-produced values and avoids directly naming some of those model types.
outcomes: The `flows` module owns a type-rich implementation with a broader direct model import surface.
The `flows` module has a narrower import surface and relies on provider APIs for some decisions.
witness.observer: The generated `flows` module, dependency graph, and later agents implementing proof and activation behavior
